cues.zh: 人们期望计算机在处理数字时完全准确、精确。
cues.en: People expect computers to be entirely accurate and precise with numbers.

cues.zh: 你从小就用计算器，自然会期望输入：
cues.en: You know, you grow up with calculators. You expect that if you type in:
"0.1 + 0.2", you expect it to come out to "0.3".

cues.zh: 每个程序员在学习过程中，迟早都会
cues.en: And sooner or later every programmer, as they're learning,

cues.zh: 尝试类似的事情。他们把它输入编程语言。
cues.en: tries something like that. And they type it into a programming language.

cues.zh: 比如输入“0.1 + 0.2”，然后按下回车，
cues.en: Something like "0.1 + 0.2", and they will hit Enter,

cues.zh: 计算机给出的结果会是类似“0.300000000...1”。
cues.en: and what the computer will give them is something like "0.300000000...1".

cues.zh: 这时，他们就开始了解浮点数了，
cues.en: And at that point, they will have started to learn about floating point numbers,

cues.zh: 也开始抓狂了。
cues.en: and they will be starting to tear their hair out.

cues.zh: 浮点数本质上就是科学记数法。
cues.en: Floating point numbers are essentially scientific notation.

cues.zh: 给不了解的人解释一下，假设你是天体物理学家，
cues.en: For the uninitiated, let's say you're an astrophysicist,

cues.zh: 你手上有光速，
cues.en: and you have the speed of light,

cues.zh: 那是一个后面跟着八个0的巨大数字。
cues.en: which is this enormous number with eight 0s after it.

cues.zh: 你想把它乘以一个很小的距离。
cues.en: And you want to multiply it by a tiny distance.

cues.zh: 我们在这里测量什么其实并不重要，它只是一个大数和一个小数。
cues.en: It doesn't really matter what we're measuring here, it's just a big number and a small number.

cues.zh: 假设你想把这两个数相乘。（我可能故意把这个弄得简单了点。）
cues.en: Let's say you want to multiply these two together. (I may have made this a bit deliberately easy.)

cues.zh: 你可以试着做一些非常复杂的数学运算把它算出来，
cues.en: You could try and do some really complicated maths and work it all out,

cues.zh: 但你不需要这么做。因为用科学记数法，
cues.en: but you don't need to. Because in scientific notation,

cues.zh: 这个数是 3 乘以 10 的 8 次方，
cues.en: this is 3 times 10 to the 8,

cues.zh: 而这个数是 1.5 乘以 10 的 -7 次方。
cues.en: and this one is 1.5 times 10 to the -7.

cues.zh: 所以把这两个数相乘，你不需要做任何特别复杂的事情。
cues.en: So you don't need to do anything particularly complicated to multiply these two together.

cues.zh: 你只需要把它们相乘，得到 4.5，
cues.en: All you have to do is multiply these, which is 4.5,

cues.zh: 然后把这些指数相加。
cues.en: and then add these exponents together here.

cues.zh: 所以，8 加 -7，8 减 7 等于 1。
cues.en: So, 8 add -7, eight minus seven means that's 1.

cues.zh: 于是我们得到 4.5 乘以 10 的 1 次方，也就是 4.5 乘以 10，即 45。
cues.en: So we'll have 4.5 times 10 to the 1, or 4.5 times 10, or 45.

cues.zh: 太棒了。这比真正去处理大数要容易多了。
cues.en: Brilliant. That's much easier than trying to actually handle large numbers.

cues.zh: 这也引出了有效数字的概念。
cues.en: And it also brings us to the concept of significant figures.

cues.zh: 因为光速并不是正好 3 乘以 10 的 8 次方。
cues.en: Because the speed of light isn't exactly 3 times 10 to the 8.

cues.zh: 而是 2.997 几几几，后面还有一大堆数字
cues.en: It's 2.997[something], and there's a lot of digits on the end of there

cues.zh: 这些数字在日常计算中其实无关紧要。
cues.en: which don't really matter for everyday calculations.

cues.zh: 我们把它四舍五入，说它是 3 乘以 10 的 8 次方。
cues.en: We round it up. We say it's 3 times 10 to the 8.

cues.zh: 或者，为了精确起见，我们说它是 2.997 乘以 10 的 8 次方，
cues.en: Or maybe, for being precise, we say it's 2.997 times 10 to the 8,

cues.zh: 但我们并不真的在意后面那些数字。
cues.en: but we don't really worry about the numbers beyond that.

cues.zh: 先记住这一点。我们稍后再回来说有效数字。
cues.en: Hold that thought. So, we'll come back to significant digits later.

cues.zh: 浮点数的两大主要优势是速度和效率。
cues.en: The two main advantages to floating point are speed and efficiency.

cues.zh: 速度快，是因为浮点数经过了长年累月的构建。
cues.en: Speed, because floating point has been built over many, many years.

cues.zh: 现在计算机处理起来快如闪电。
cues.en: It is now lightning fast for computers to deal with.

cues.zh: 还有效率，因为它能处理非常大的数字——
cues.en: And efficiency, because it can deal with really big numbers --

cues.zh: 巨大的数字，宇宙尺度的数字——
cues.en: massive numbers, "size of the universe" numbers --

cues.zh: 以及非常小的数字——原子尺度的数字——
cues.en: and really small numbers -- "size of an atom" numbers --

cues.zh: 而不需要占用海量空间。
cues.en: without needing enormous amounts of space.

cues.zh: 如果你的格式需要同时容纳宇宙的大小
cues.en: If you had a format that needed to include the size of the universe

cues.zh: 和原子的大小，那你就得在两端存储多得离谱的零
cues.en: and the size of an atom, you'd need so many zeroes stored on both ends

cues.zh: 或者需要某种特别复杂的机制让计算机去计算
cues.en: or you'd need something particularly complicated for a computer to work out

cues.zh: 结果要么效率极低，存一个数就要一兆字节，
cues.en: that it would either be really inefficient, storing one number as a megabyte,

cues.zh: 要么需要某种对计算机来说极其繁琐的东西
cues.en: or you would need something that would be really fiddly for a computer

cues.zh: 去处理所有零和数字的摆放位置。
cues.en: to work out as it tries to place all the zeroes and the numbers everywhere.

cues.zh: 我们来聊聊十进制。聊聊我们人类。
cues.en: Let's talk about base 10. Let's talk about us - people.

cues.zh: （顺便说下灯突然全亮了。真奇怪。）
cues.en: (Let's talk about the lights being on all of a sudden. That's weird.)

cues.zh: 在十进制中，在我们日常使用的人类数字里，
cues.en: In base 10, in our normal human numbers,

cues.zh: 也就是你知道的十个数字——十进制，
cues.en: so you know ten digits - base 10,

cues.zh: 我们有百位、十位和个位。这是小学就学过的。
cues.en: we have hundreds, tens, and units. You learn that in primary school.

cues.zh: 而这边，有十分位、百分位和千分位。
cues.en: And over here, you have tenths, hundredths, and thousandths.

cues.zh: 所以如果你想用小数表示“十分之一”，你会说“0.1”，
cues.en: So if you want to say "one tenth" in decimal, you say "0.1",

cues.zh: 这很正常，也很自然。
cues.en: and that's normal, and that's natural.

cues.zh: 但二进制呢，计算机……它们不是这样做的。
cues.en: Base 2, on the other hand, binary..., computers..., they don't do that.

cues.zh: 因为它们看到的是四、二和一。
cues.en: Because what they see are fours, twos, and ones.

cues.zh: 然后这边是：二分之一、四分之一、八分之一和十六分之一。
cues.en: And then over here: halves, quarters, eighths and sixteenths.

cues.zh: 这里面没有0.1。
cues.en: There's no 0.1 in there.

cues.zh: 事实上，0.1在二进制中是“0.00011”，而那个“0011”是循环的。
cues.en: In fact, 0.1 in binary is "0.00011", and that "0011" is recurring.
It's actually 0.00011001100110011... all the way to infinity.

cues.zh: 这很有意思，因为32位计算机，
cues.en: Which is interesting, because 32-bit computers,

cues.zh: 我们通常用的那些（现在我们已经有所进步了）
cues.en: the ones we generally use, (we've moved a bit on now)

cues.zh: 32位计算机只存储23位有效数字。
cues.en: 32-bit computers only store 23 significant digits.

cues.zh: 它们还会存储小数点的位置。
cues.en: They also store where the decimal point is.

cues.zh: 它们本质上是以2为底的科学计数法。这就是浮点数的含义。
cues.en: They basically do scientific notation in base 2. That's what floating point is.

cues.zh: 于是它们说：“好吧，我们得到了这个很长的二进制数，
cues.en: So they say, "All right, so we've got this long binary number,

cues.zh: 乘以2的某次方。”
cues.en: times 2 to the something."

cues.zh: 这就是问题所在。因为它损失的是精度。
cues.en: And that's a problem. Because what it loses is precision.

cues.zh: 它不理解递归。
cues.en: It doesn't understand recursion.

cues.zh: 我用十进制来打个比方：
cues.en: I have an analogy for that in base 10:

cues.zh: 如果你试着把“三分之一”写成小数，我们会这样：
cues.en: if you try to write "a third" as a decimal, we go:

cues.zh: 百位、十位、个位、十分位、百分位、千分位，
cues.en: hundreds, tens, units, tenths, hundredths, thousandths,

cues.zh: 然后我们试着算下去，结果得到0.333333333……循环。
cues.en: and then, we try and do this and we end up with 0.333333333... recurring.

cues.zh: 现在想象你不理解循环小数，就像计算机一样，
cues.en: Now imagine you don't understand recurring numbers, like a computer,

cues.zh: 就像科学计数法，如果你去掉那个递归，
cues.en: like scientific notation if you take away that recursion,

cues.zh: 就像浮点运算那样不理解。
cues.en: like floating point arithmetic doesn't.

cues.zh: 所以这就是我们把一切串起来的地方。
cues.en: So this is where we bring everything together.

cues.zh: 在十进制里，假设你有 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3。
cues.en: If you're in base 10, if you're in decimal, let's say you have 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3.

cues.zh: 我们人类会说：“那就是 0.3 循环，加 0.3 循环，
cues.en: As humans we go, "Well that's 0.3 recurring, plus 0.3 recurring,

cues.zh: 加 0.3 循环，等于 1。”
cues.en: plus 0.3 recurring, which is 1."

cues.zh: 但假如你是台计算机，你不懂循环小数，
cues.en: But say you're a computer and you don't understand recursion,

cues.zh: 因为浮点运算本质上是有效数字。
cues.en: because floating point math is essentially significant figures.

cues.zh: 所以计算机会看着它说：“0.333333333……
cues.en: So a computer would look at that and go, "0.333333333...
plus 333..., plus 333...", and it will say,

cues.zh: “三分之一加三分之一加三分之一，加起来是 0.99999999……”
cues.en: "Well, a third plus a third plus a third. Total it to 0.99999999..."

cues.zh: 但过一会儿你就得停，因为位数用完了。
cues.en: But after a while, you'll stop. Because you've run out of digits.

cues.zh: 你得到的就是浮点舍入误差。
cues.en: What you've just got there is a floating point rounding error.

cues.zh: 再降到二进制看看。算一下 1/10 + 2/10。
cues.en: Let's take it down again to base 2. Let's do 1/10 + 2/10.
Which is 0.00011001100110011... Oh! We've run out of digits!

cues.zh: 因为32位计算机的浮点运算只存23位数字。
cues.en: Because floating point arithmetic on 32-bit computers only stores 23 digits.
And then you try and add 2/10, which is 0.001100110011...

cues.zh: 我不打算真去算这个，因为那要花好久，
cues.en: I'm not going to try and do that maths, because it's going to take ages

cues.zh: 但结果和这边完全一样。
cues.en: but what happens is exactly the same as back here.

cues.zh: 在32位运算里到23位之后（我记得64位计算机上是56位）
cues.en: After 23 digits in 32-bit arithmetic (I think we've got 56 on 64-bit computers)

cues.zh: 就截断了。它不懂循环小数，
cues.en: it cuts. It doesn't understand recurring,

cues.zh: 所以浮点数看到1/10 + 2/10，也就是你刚输入的那个，
cues.en: which means that floating point looks at 1/10 + 2/10, what you just typed in,
"0.1 + 0.2" in decimal, and it says that 1/10 + 2/10

cues.zh: 并不完全等于3/10。
cues.en: does NOT quite equal 3/10.

cues.zh: 因为在它看来，就是不等于。
cues.en: Because, to its mind, it doesn't.

cues.zh: 几乎所有情况下，它都足够接近了。
cues.en: For nearly all cases, it IS close enough.

cues.zh: 大多数情况下，你不需要超过23位二进制小数的精度。
cues.en: In most cases, you don't need more than 23 binary digits of precision.

cues.zh: 如果需要，你就上64位。
cues.en: If you do, you go to 64-bit.

cues.zh: 如果你在做3D游戏，需要知道屏幕上某个东西该指向哪里，
cues.en: If you are doing a 3D game and you need to know where to point something on the screen,

cues.zh: 就算偏了十万分之一像素也没关系
cues.en: it doesn't matter if it's 1/100000 of a pixel out

cues.zh: 因为它会落在正确的位置上。
cues.en: because it will be in the right place.

cues.zh: 如果你在做大规模计算，就算差了极小极小极小的一个零头——
cues.en: And if you're doing big calculations, it doesn't matter if a tiny, tiny, tiny fraction --

cues.zh: 比分子还小的一个零头——也没关系，
cues.en: something smaller than a molecule -- is out,

cues.zh: 因为它看起来大致是对的：
cues.en: because it will look more or less right:

cues.zh: 其精确度远超现实世界所能达到的任何精度或容差。
cues.en: right beyond any precision or tolerance that the real world could possibly manage.

cues.zh: 但这意味着，如果你在处理货币，你说
cues.en: But it means that if you're dealing with currency, and you say that

cues.zh: 你在把10便士（或0.1英镑）加到20便士上，每个程序员迟早都会碰到这个问题，
cues.en: you are adding 10p (or £0.1) to 20p, every programmer hits this sooner or later,

cues.zh: 我们就这么一算。很简单。
cues.en: we just go like that. That's easy.

cues.zh: 计算机却会回来说：“其实是……这么多便士。”
cues.en: A computer will come back and say, "That's actually... that many pence."

cues.zh: 而在这些具体的人类事务上，我们会注意到这个错误
cues.en: And in these particular human things, we will notice the error

cues.zh: 因为突然间，对我们来说这变得非常非常明显。
cues.en: because suddenly to us it's very, very obvious.

cues.zh: 这就是浮点数的问题。顺便说一下，要解决这个问题，如果你在处理货币，
cues.en: That's the problem with floating point. To fix that, by the way, if you're doing currency,

cues.zh: 要么用更高级编程语言里的十进制类型
cues.en: you either use a decimal type in more advanced programming languages

cues.zh: 要么就全部以整数存储，单位用便士、美分之类的
cues.en: or you just store everything as an integer in terms of pence, cents, or whatever

cues.zh: 最后再除以100。
cues.en: and then divide by 100 at the end.

cues.zh: 浮点数确实让很多人非常困惑。
cues.en: Floating point is something that really, really confuses a lot of people.

cues.zh: 很难理解，直到你意识到它其实就是科学计数法。
cues.en: It's tough to get your head around until you realize that it is just scientific notation.

cues.zh: 跟我们在学校数学课上学的是一样的，只不过是以2为底。
cues.en: It's the same thing that we learned in maths class at school, only in base 2.

cues.zh: 就是二分之一、四分之一、八分之一，
cues.en: It's halves and quarters and eighths,

cues.zh: 一旦你搞懂了这一点，一旦你意识到它存储的是固定长度的数字
cues.en: and once you crack that, once you realize that it's storing a set length of number

cues.zh: 然后算出小数点该在哪，其实就是有效数字，
cues.en: and then working out where the decimal point could be and it's just significant figures,

cues.zh: 就开始变得容易多了。然后你就会明白，
cues.en: it starts to become a lot easier. And you start to realize,

cues.zh: “哦，这就是为什么我输入0.1 + 0.2，得到的不是0.3。”
cues.en: "Oh, that's why if i type 0.1 + 0.2, what I get isn't 0.3."
